{{Short description|American demographer (born 1949)}}
'''Amy Ong Tsui''' (born 1949) is an American demographer.  

Due to the [[Chinese Civil War]], Tsui's father emigrated to the United States to pursue doctoral studies in agricultural economics. Tsui was born in [[Pullman, Washington]] in 1949. The elder Tsui worked for the [[Food and Agriculture Organization]] and moved his family to Bangladesh and Thailand. The Tsui family later returned to the United States. Amy complted high school, attended [[Carlton College]] in Minnesota, transferred to the [[University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa]], completing a BA (1970) and MA (1972), and a PhD (1977) at the [[University of Chicago]]; [[Donald Bogue]] was her advisor).<ref name="paainterview"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Madren |first1=Carrie |title=Understanding human population change with Amy Ong Tsui |url=https://www.aaas.org/understanding-human-population-change-amy-ong-tsui |access-date=20 August 2023 |publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science |date=29 July 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Watts |first1=Geoff |title=Amy Tsui: population expert for whom people count |journal=The Lancet |date=14 July 2012 |volume=380 |issue=9837 |page=100 |doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(12)61164-7|doi-access=free |pmid=22794232 }}</ref> 

Tsui remained on faculty at Chicago until 1982, before joining faculty at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Amy Tsui |url=https://www.populationassociation.org/support/honored-members/amy-tsui |access-date=20 August 2023 |publisher=Population Association of America}}</ref><ref name="paainterview">{{cite news |url=https://higherlogicdownload.s3.amazonaws.com/POPULATIONASSOCIATION/3e04a602-09fe-49d8-93e4-1dd0069a7f14/UploadedImages/Past_President_Interviews/80_Amy_Tsui.pdf |access-date=20 August 2023 |date=2003}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=AAAS Elects Six Johns Hopkins Faculty Members as Fellows |url=https://pages.jh.edu/gazette/2003/03nov03/03elects.html |access-date=20 August 2023 |work=The Presidents 1931–Present |url=https://www.populationassociation.org/about/officers-directors/past-presidents |access-date=20 August 2023 |publisher=Population Association of America}}</ref> She also collaborated with universities in various [[Africa|African]] countries in improving their own population and reproductive health departments.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Understanding human population |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260115145625/https://www.demographic-research.org/articles/articlesbyauthor/12879 |archive-date=2026-01-15 |access-date=2026-02-27 |website=Demographic Research |language=en}}</ref>

Early in her career, she and Bogue challenged the notion of the "[[population bomb]]," predicting that increasing contraceptive use would cause the global population to balance at 8 billion by 2050.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Understanding human population change with Amy Ong Tsui {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) |url=https://www.aaas.org/taxonomy/term/4/understanding-human-population-change-amy-ong-tsui |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250705004752/https://www.aaas.org/taxonomy/term/4/understanding-human-population-change-amy-ong-tsui |archive-date=2025-07-05 |access-date=2026-03-06 |website=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) |language=en}}</ref> In most recent years, Tsui has focused her research on the topic of women's reproductive activities, prenatal care, and contraceptive usage in various countries around the world.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amy O Tsui |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=m_TVZlkAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=sra |access-date=2025-02-16 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Zerai |first1=Assata |last2=Tsui |first2=Amy Ong |date=August 2001 |title=The Relationship between Prenatal Care and Subsequent Modern Contraceptive Use in Bolivia, Egypt and Thailand |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3583432 |journal=African Journal of Reproductive Health |volume=5 |issue=2 |pages=68 |doi=10.2307/3583432 |jstor=3583432 |pmid=12471915 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
